title: Recovery Services vaults and Backup vaults
learningObjective: Create and set up Recovery Services vaults and Backup vaults, and pick the right vault for each kind of data.

prerequisites.text: Azure VMs, storage accounts and disks basics

foundation: Azure Backup stores recovery points in a vault, a management container with its own storage.
There are two vault types: Recovery Services vaults (VMs, SQL in VMs, Azure Files, on-premises, and Site Recovery) and Backup vaults (newer workloads such as blobs, disks, PostgreSQL and AKS).
engineer: Where to create the vault: in the same region as what it protects. (For Site Recovery, in the target region.)
Vault storage redundancy: GRS (default), LRS or ZRS. You can only change it before the first item is protected.
Cross Region Restore (CRR): lets you restore in the paired region. Needs GRS, and you must turn it on.

Vault security: soft delete, which keeps deleted backups 14 days by default and can be longer or always on; immutable vaults, where nobody can shorten retention or delete recovery points; multi-user authorization with Resource Guard, so critical actions need a second person; encryption with platform keys or your own keys; private endpoints.

Which vault for what: a Recovery Services vault for Azure VMs, SQL and SAP HANA in VMs, Azure Files, and Site Recovery; a Backup vault for Azure Blobs (operational and vaulted), Azure Disks (snapshots), Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server, AKS, and others in the support matrix.
One view of both: Business continuity center shows both vault types together.
Roles: Backup Contributor, manages everything; Backup Operator, backs up and restores but can't delete; Backup Reader, view only.
Backup vault identities: a Backup vault uses a managed identity, which needs roles on what it protects (for example Disk Backup Reader).

example.title: One region, two vaults
body: Contoso protects its VMs and file shares with rsv-prod-eus (GRS with Cross Region Restore). It protects its managed disks and blob containers with bv-prod-eus. Both use soft delete and immutability. Deleting backup data needs approval through Resource Guard.

prerequisites: An Azure subscription with VMs to monitor or protect
permissions: Backup Contributor to manage vaults and policies (Monitoring Contributor for alerts and diagnostic settings)
limits: Vault redundancy can't change once items are protected
The vault must be in the same region as what it protects (Azure Backup)
portal: Create a resource > Recovery Services vault (or Backup vault): subscription, resource group, name, region.
Vault > Properties > Backup configuration: storage redundancy and Cross Region Restore (before protecting items).
Vault > Properties > Security settings: soft delete, immutability, multi-user authorization.
configuration.cli:
az backup vault create -g rg-bkp -n rsv-prod-eus -l eastus
az backup vault backup-properties set -g rg-bkp -n rsv-prod-eus --backup-storage-redundancy GeoRedundant --cross-region-restore-flag true
az dataprotection backup-vault create -g rg-bkp --vault-name bv-prod-eus -l eastus --type SystemAssigned --storage-settings datastore-type=VaultStore type=GeoRedundant
configuration.powershell:
New-AzRecoveryServicesVault -ResourceGroupName rg-bkp -Name rsv-prod-eus -Location eastus
$v = Get-AzRecoveryServicesVault -ResourceGroupName rg-bkp -Name rsv-prod-eus
Set-AzRecoveryServicesBackupProperty -Vault $v -BackupStorageRedundancy GeoRedundant
$s = New-AzDataProtectionBackupVaultStorageSettingObject -DataStoreType VaultStore -Type GeoRedundant
New-AzDataProtectionBackupVault -ResourceGroupName rg-bkp -VaultName bv-prod-eus -Location eastus -StorageSetting $s

lab.objective: Choose the right vault for every data source.
steps: Open the 'Recovery Services vault or Backup vault' tab.
Answer every data source and read the explanation.
expected: VMs, SQL in VMs, Files, MARS → RSV
Blobs, Disks, PostgreSQL, AKS → Backup vault
failureScenarios: Using a Backup vault for VMs
lab.cost: None. The simulation runs entirely in the browser.

troubleshooting.symptom: You can't change the vault's storage redundancy.
troubleshooting.fix: Stop protection and delete the data, or create a new vault.

troubleshooting.symptom: A VM doesn't appear when you set up backup.
troubleshooting.cause: The vault is in a different region.
troubleshooting.fix: Create a vault in the VM's region.

troubleshooting.symptom: Disk backup fails with a permissions error.
troubleshooting.cause: The Backup vault's identity is missing roles.
troubleshooting.fix: Give it Disk Backup Reader and Disk Snapshot Contributor.

comparisons.difference: AWS has one kind of vault for every service. Azure has two vault types, split by workload.
Also uses Recovery Services vaults, but for copying and failing over VMs, not for backups.

misconceptions.myth: One vault can protect resources in any region.
misconceptions.reality: No. A vault protects resources in its own region.

misconceptions.myth: Soft delete can't be turned off.
misconceptions.reality: It can, unless it's set to always on.

architectureDecisions: Production that must survive a region outage: use GRS and Cross Region Restore.
Protect against ransomware: turn on immutability and multi-user authorization.
Separate vaults: one per environment and region.

Soft delete and other security features

steps.label: Where do backups go?
steps.title: You need backups, but which vault?
body: Azure Backup stores recovery points in a vault. There are two vault types, and each protects different things.

steps.label: RSV
steps.title: Recovery Services vault
body: Protects Azure VMs, SQL Server and SAP HANA in VMs, Azure Files, on-premises machines (MARS agent, MABS) and is also used by Azure Site Recovery.

steps.label: Backup vault
steps.title: Backup vault
body: The newer vault type for Azure Disks, Azure Blobs, Azure Database for PostgreSQL, AKS and similar workloads.

callout.text: Backing up managed disks directly (not the whole VM) uses a Backup vault.

steps.label: Settings
steps.title: Decide before the first backup
body: Create the vault in the same region as the resources it protects. Backup storage redundancy (GRS by default, or LRS / ZRS) can only be changed before you protect the first item. Enable cross-region restore if you need to restore in the paired region.

steps.label: Security
steps.title: Protect the backups themselves
body: Soft delete keeps deleted backup data for 14 days (or longer). Immutability prevents early deletion of recovery points. Multi-user authorization needs a second person's approval for critical operations.

steps.label: Recap
steps.title: Vaults
body: Right vault, right region, settings first.
recap: RSV: VMs, SQL/SAP HANA in VMs, Azure Files, on-premises, Site Recovery
Backup vault: disks, blobs, PostgreSQL, AKS
Same region as the protected resources

handsOn.title: Create both vault types and review their settings
before: Signed in at portal.azure.com as Owner of a subscription (a free or pay-as-you-go account works). Work in a resource group called rg-az104-lab.
If rg-az104-lab does not exist yet: search 'Resource groups' > Create > name rg-az104-lab, region UAE North (or any region near you) > Review + create > Create.

steps.do: Search 'Recovery Services vaults' > + Create. Group rg-az104-lab, name rsv-lab, region UAE North (or any region near you). Create.
Open rsv-lab > Settings > Properties > Backup configuration > Update.
steps.see: Storage replication type: Geo-redundant by default, with Locally and Zone-redundant options. Change it to Locally-redundant and Save (allowed because nothing is protected yet).

steps.do: Still in Properties, open Security settings.
steps.see: Soft delete (on, 14 days) and immutability options.
Workloads you can protect: Azure (VMs, Azure Files, SQL Server in Azure VM, SAP HANA) and on-premises.

steps.do: Search 'Backup vaults' > + Create. Group rg-az104-lab, name bv-lab, region UAE North (or any region near you), redundancy Locally-redundant. Create.

steps.see: Datasource types such as Azure Disks, Azure Blobs and Azure Database for PostgreSQL.
Both vaults listed in one place.

check: You changed rsv-lab's redundancy before any backup, and saw what each vault protects.
cleanup: Keep rsv-lab for the next lab, or: When you finish for the day: Resource groups > rg-az104-lab > Delete resource group > type the name > Delete. This removes everything inside it.
